oneLiner: Peak-cycle memory printing 85% gross margins on an AI-driven DRAM/HBM shortage, back above $1,000 a share at roughly 6.5x forward earnings that the market still refuses to capitalize.
thesis: One of three companies able to manufacture leading-edge DRAM at scale; HBM4 qualified into NVIDIA-class platforms with more than $1B already shipped and a ramp tracking twice as fast as HBM3E.

HBM is fully sold out for calendar 2026 under multi-year fixed-price contracts: 16 take-or-pay agreements representing roughly $100B of floor-price revenue convert cyclical pricing into something closer to backlog.
Q3 FY2026 revenue $41.5B (versus $9.3B a year earlier) with 85% gross margin and $18.3B of quarterly free cash flow: earnings power without precedent in memory history.

The whole question is durability, and the first crack in the price curve is visible: TrendForce has Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices rising 13-18% QoQ, a sharp deceleration from the 90%+ moves earlier in the cycle, with consumer buyers at their affordability limit.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 FY2026 (ended May 28, 2026; reported Jun 24, 2026)
points: Revenue $41.46B, ~+346% YoY; GAAP gross margin 84.6%; operating margin 80.4%.
Non-GAAP EPS $25.11 vs ~$20.49 consensus; adjusted FCF $18.3B.
Guide: Q4 FY2026 revenue $50.0B plus or minus $1B, gross margin ~86%, EPS $31.00 plus or minus $1.
DRAM $31.3B (76% of revenue); cloud memory BU $13.8B; roughly $100B of long-term customer agreements referenced.
HBM sold out for calendar 2026; more than $1B of HBM4 shipped; targets HBM share equal to overall DRAM share.

segments: DRAM ~76% of revenue, NAND ~24%. By business unit: cloud memory $13.8B, core data center $11.5B, mobile/client $11.5B, auto/embedded $4.6B.
HBM is the strategic prize: HBM4 ramping now, HBM4E in 2027. Twelve-layer HBM4 is reported to move from 20-30% of Micron's HBM output early in 2026 to as much as half by year-end.
competitive: HBM share remains contested and tracker-dependent: one Q2 2026 read puts SK Hynix at 50%, Samsung 32% and Micron 18%; another has SK hynix near 62% with Micron having passed Samsung.

Scale is the structural gap: Samsung and SK Hynix each run roughly 150,000-200,000 HBM wafers a month, three to four times Micron's base. Micron is reported to be doubling to about 100,000 wafers a month by end-2026.
NAND: fifth place (~11% share) behind Samsung, SK Hynix, Kioxia and Sandisk.
CXMT (China) hit 7.6% of global DRAM in Q1 2026 and IPO'd at roughly $85B; not yet at the leading edge.
Reported that NVIDIA is testing leaner memory specifications on some platforms - a modest spec-down risk to content per accelerator (unverified).
moat: Leading-edge DRAM process capability (1-beta/1-gamma), HBM4 qualification into the dominant AI platform, and take-or-pay contracts with floor pricing that convert spot into contracted revenue. Breadth across HBM, LPDDR, DDR5 and QLC NAND lets wafers chase the highest return. The binding limit is capacity, not demand: management has said it can fill only half to two thirds of HBM demand.
risks: Peak-cycle earnings: 85% gross margins are unprecedented and mean-reverting; the price curve is already flattening (Q3 2026 contract prices +13-18% QoQ versus 90%+ earlier).
Consumer demand destruction: TrendForce flags PC and smartphone buyers hitting their price tolerance, which is how memory upcycles usually end.
Capacity gap: Samsung and SK Hynix add capacity from a base three to four times larger; SK Hynix is targeting an ~8x 1c DRAM ramp.
CXMT share gains (7.6% and rising) plus reports of Apple qualifying CXMT parts.
HBM4 execution against SK Hynix's allocation lead, and any spec-down of memory content per accelerator.
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 earnings in late September 2026 (guide: $50B revenue, ~86% gross margin, $31 EPS) plus the first FY2027 framing.
HBM4 multi-customer qualifications through H2 2026; HBM4E volume in 2027.
Calendar-2027 HBM contract and pricing announcements.
TrendForce Q4 2026 contract-price prints - the cleanest read on whether the deceleration continues.
pricedIn: The stock closed at $1,016.59 on Sep 4, 2026, up 6% on the day and back above $1,000, but still about 16% below the $1,213.37 all-time closing high set Jun 25. That is roughly 6.5x forward and ~23x trailing earnings against an industry median near 30x: the market is refusing to capitalize peak earnings at any multiple. Debate: a single-digit multiple on peak EPS is exactly what a cycle top looks like, and CXMT plus a flattening price curve give the bears their entry - against which sits sold-out fixed-price HBM and $100B of take-or-pay floors that make this cycle's earnings more durable than any before it.

scenarios.bear: FY2026 is the peak: contract price increases fade through 2027 as competitor capacity lands from a far larger base, consumer demand stays destroyed, CXMT floods conventional DRAM, margins compress toward the 50s, EPS halves, and the stock de-rates the way every prior memory cycle ended.
scenarios.base: Q4 hits roughly $50B and $31 of EPS; calendar-2027 HBM is largely pre-sold at firm prices, cushioning a moderating conventional curve; earnings plateau rather than collapse; the stock holds a trillion-dollar-class market cap with violent cycle-headline volatility.
scenarios.bull: The HBM TAM crosses $100B in 2027 with tightness beyond; Micron's capacity doubling lands and holds 20%+ share into HBM4 and HBM4E; NAND scarcity adds a second leg; the 6-7x multiple re-rates toward 8-10x as the market accepts a structurally higher earnings floor.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: at roughly 6.5x forward P/E the market is pricing a memory downcycle, and the reverse DCF quantifies the implied annual earnings decline. Bear equals a deep downcycle (prior cycles saw EPS halve or worse); bull is the structural-shortage case where earnings hold and grow.

latestProse: Q3 FY2026 (ended May 28; reported Jun 24). Revenue $41.46B versus $9.30B a year earlier (+346%); GAAP gross margin 84.6%, operating margin 80.4% (operating income $33.7B). Non-GAAP EPS $25.11 against ~$20.49 consensus; adjusted free cash flow $18.3B in the quarter. DRAM was $31.3B, 76% of revenue; the cloud memory unit alone did $13.8B. HBM is sold out for calendar 2026 and more than $1B of HBM4 has shipped. The disclosure that matters most: 16 take-or-pay agreements covering roughly $100B of floor-price revenue - the contractual floor is the entire argument against valuing this as a normal cycle top.
guidanceProse: Q4 FY2026 guide: revenue $50.0B plus or minus $1B, gross margin ~86%, EPS $31.00 plus or minus $1 on roughly 1.15B shares, with the report due in late September. Management can fill only half to two thirds of HBM demand and sees the HBM TAM crossing $100B in 2027. The offsetting signal since the last update is pricing: TrendForce has Q3 2026 DRAM contract prices up 13-18% QoQ, a sharp deceleration from earlier in the cycle, with consumer buyers at the limit of what they will pay even as AI server demand holds. The market pays about 6.5x forward earnings for the combination.
